title: Leaving professionally with Buzzin' Harris's TOBA vaudeville show
summary: A touring show's pianist fell ill; she memorised the whole show from the owner's humming and played that night. She toured Ohio and Indiana for two months with comedian Brodson (Buzzin') Harris's weekly TOBA vaudeville.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: talent show then. The first time I left really professionally is when a show came to Pittsburgh and the pianist, something happened to him so the Western Union boy hdd delivered a wire to the owner of the show. The owner told him, "My goodness, I need a pianist. I've got to go out..." He said, "I know who you should get, the little piano girl." He said, "What?" He said, "Come and go with me, I'll take you to East Liberty to her house." So he brought this man all the way - about 8 miles from downtown to East Liberty. When the manager drove up I was on the sidewalk playing Hop Scotch with the kids. He was so angry and upset because he didn't have much time before the show that night. He said, "Why would you take up so much of my time bringing me out here?" He said, "Wait till you hear her play." So he went in and out, and he asked me if I could memorize and I said yes. He hummed the entire show to me and I memorized it. That night I played it.
Was any of it material you had heard before?

Nothing I had heard before - Bandanna Days and all that kind of thing, I had never heard them before. You know during that period they were all tunes like that, like old-fashioned, like, I don't know what you'd call them, but they were like minstrel show tunes, you know? So I went up - he had to go to a notary with my mother so that I'd be able to go out. It was during the summer vacation
and school was out, so my mother signed papers for me to go out with a lady. I worked with him about two months until school opened in September.
I went to all these little cities like Springfield, Ohio, Springfield something, Indianapolis -
What kind of a show was this?
Vaudeville, the worst...T.O.B.A, you've heard of that. Tough On Black Actors.
He was the owner of the show.
Yes, he was a comedian, a very good one, a black-face comedian.
